Math

Here we describe the mathematical framework of the DALI formalism.

Inner product

All inner products are defined as

\[\langle a | b \rangle = 4 \, \Delta f \, \sum_{i} \Re \left[ \frac{\tilde{a}(f_i) \tilde{b}^*(f_i)}{S_n(f_i)} \right],\]

where \(\tilde{a}(f)\) and \(\tilde{b}(f)\) are the Fourier transforms of the time-domain signals and \(\Delta f\) is the size of the frequency bin. There is always a minimum frequency, maximum frequency and a grid resolution. These can be adjusted to the user’s preferences in the options of the functions SNR and DALITensors.

DALI tensors

The DALI Likelihood expansion, up to derivative order 3, is defined as

\[\begin{split}\ln \mathcal{L}(\theta) = &- \frac{1}{2} \langle h_i | h_j \rangle \Delta \theta^{i j} \\ &-\left( \frac{1}{2! 1!} \langle h_{ij} | h_k \rangle \Delta \theta^{i j k} + \frac{1}{2 \, 2!^2} \langle h_{ij} | h_{kl} \rangle \Delta \theta^{i j k l} \right) \\ &-\left( \frac{1}{3! 1!} \langle h_{ijk} | h_l \rangle \Delta \theta^{i j k l} + \frac{1}{3! 2!} \langle h_{ijk} | h_{lm} \rangle \Delta \theta^{i j k l m} + \frac{1}{2 \, 3!^2} \langle h_{ijk} | h_{lmn} \rangle \Delta \theta^{i j k l m n} \right),\end{split}\]

where \(\Delta \theta^{i_1 ... i_N } = \Delta \theta^{i_1} ... \Delta \theta^{i_N}\). It can be proved that the order N contribution to the DALI expansion is given by

\[\frac{1}{N! 1!} \langle h_{i_1 ... i_N} | h_{j_1} \rangle \Delta \theta^{i_1 ... i_N j_1} + \dots + \frac{1}{2 \, N!^2} \langle h_{i_1 ... i_N} | h_{j_1 ... j_N} \rangle \Delta \theta^{i_1 ... i_N j_1 ... j_N}.\]

SymDALI can calculate the DALI tensors up to derivative order N=4 with the function DALITensors.

In the case of a network of detectors all DALI tensors are summed over the detectors:

\[\begin{split}&\langle h_i | h_j \rangle = \sum_a \langle h_i | h_j \rangle_a \\ &\langle h_i | h_{j k} \rangle = \sum_a \langle h_i | h_{j k} \rangle_a \\ & \qquad \qquad \dots,\end{split}\]

where the inner product with subscript \(a\) is the usual inner product calculated with the noise power spectral density of the \(a\)-th detector.

Taylor form

Taylor form refers to the grouping of the terms in the DALI expansion in powers of \(\Delta \theta^i\). This form is useful for sampling the likelihood, as it allows for a more efficient evaluation algorithm. For instance, to derivative order N=3 the Taylor Form would be

\[\begin{split}\ln \mathcal{L}(\theta) = &- \frac{1}{2} \langle h_i | h_j \rangle \Delta \theta^{i j} \\ &-\frac{1}{2! 1!} \langle h_{ij} | h_k \rangle \Delta \theta^{i j k} \\ &-\left(\frac{1}{2 \, 2!^2} \langle h_{ij} | h_{kl} \rangle + \frac{1}{3! 1!} \langle h_{ijk} | h_l \rangle \right) \, \Delta \theta^{i j k l} \\ &-\frac{1}{3! 2!} \langle h_{ijk} | h_{lm} \rangle \Delta \theta^{i j k l m} \\ &-\frac{1}{2 \, 3!^2} \langle h_{ijk} | h_{lmn} \rangle \Delta \theta^{i j k l m n} + ...\end{split}\]

Once the DALI tensors are calculated, the Taylor form can be obtained with the function TaylorForm.
